turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms./Mrs. [Patient's Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go through a few important questions to ensure your safety and comfort during the procedure. Is that okay with you?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, sure, Doctor. I'm ready to answer your questions.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you. Let's start with the reason for your surgery. Can you tell me a bit about your symptoms that led to the decision for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Well, Doctor, I've been having a lot of pain in my tummy, especially after eating. The scans showed gallstones, so the doctor said it's best to remove the gallbladder.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: I see. Now, let's move on to your medications. Can you confirm the current list of medications you're taking and any allergies that have been diagnosed since your last medical review?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Okay, so I'm taking Metformin 1000 mg twice daily for my diabetes, Lisinopril 20 mg once daily for blood pressure, and Atorvastatin 40 mg once daily for cholesterol. Oh, and I also started Insulin Glargine 40 units once at night because my sugar levels were a bit high. Oh, and I have an allergy to Penicillin, which I think wasn't recorded before.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for that information. It's important we have the most up-to-date details. So, just to confirm, you're on Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, Insulin Glargine, and you have a Penicillin allergy. Is that correct?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, that's right, Doctor. And the Ranitidine was stopped, as per the doctor's advice.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Excellent. Now, regarding your NPO status, have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, Doctor. I've been fasting as instructed. Just a bit of water with my morning medications, but that was hours ago.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. Have you had any anesthesia before? If so, were there any issues or reactions?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, I had a surgery about 5 years ago. I think it was general anesthesia, and everything went smoothly. No problems at all.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great to hear. Lastly, how would you describe your overall energy levels and ability to perform daily activities? Are you able to walk up a flight of stairs without getting too breathless?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I'd say I'm fairly active, Doctor. I can walk up stairs, but sometimes I get a bit tired, especially if I've eaten a heavy meal. But generally, I manage my daily tasks without too much trouble.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that with me. It helps me understand your fitness for surgery. We'll be using general anesthesia with a Laryngeal Mask Airway and Ultrasound-Guided Regional Anesthesia for your postoperative pain management. Do you have any questions about the anesthesia plan?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, Doctor. You've explained it well. I'm just ready to get this done and feel better.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Very well. If you have any more questions later, don't hesitate to ask. We're here to ensure your surgery and recovery go as smoothly as possible.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate your care.
